name: Perform genetic and specialised tests (prenatal screening, carrier, pharmacogenomic and hereditary tests)
summary: This process turns a genetic test order and its blood or saliva sample into a signed report for the ordering provider. Laboratory assistants check consent, funding or payment and the specimen, then technologists extract DNA, run sequencing, array or genotyping batches and review the results; panels need variant classification under the ACMG and AMP rules, and a certified laboratory geneticist signs every report. Most of the elapsed time is waiting for batches to fill and for sign-out, and incomplete consent forms, unpaid private orders, no-call prenatal screens that need a new blood draw and novel variants slow individual cases.

baseline.org_archetype: The genetics laboratories (Brampton and Laval) of a large Canadian community laboratory company, offering NIPT, carrier screening, pharmacogenomics, hereditary and somatic tests, some sent to partner laboratories.
baseline.notes: The test mix is assumed: about 45 per cent prenatal screens, 15 per cent pharmacogenomic tests, 15 per cent carrier and haemoglobin gene tests, 10 per cent other in-house panels and 15 per cent send-outs to partner laboratories.

trigger: A specimen with a genetic test requisition reaches the genetics laboratory from a collection centre, clinic or online purchase.
end_state: A signed report is delivered to the ordering provider (and to the patient portal where applicable), with high-risk results phoned and referred to counselling; or the order is cancelled or closed with no result.

volume.seasonality: Fairly flat; prenatal orders follow births, slightly lower in late December.

evidence.note: Follows the organisation file's genetic orders driver (d_genetic_orders), itself an estimate.

evidence.note: Organisation file headcount 12; about three quarters of their time on order intake, accessioning, extraction and send-outs. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

Organisation file headcount 40; the rest of their time goes to validation, QC, proficiency testing and somatic work. Wage range consistent with Job Bank NOC 32120. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

steps.name: Receive specimen shipment and match it to the manifest
steps.description: A genetics laboratory assistant opens the inbound tote from the line haul or courier, checks the temperature indicator, counts tubes against the shipping manifest and scans each requisition barcode so the order shows as received in the LIS. Paper requisitions and consent or eligibility forms are scanned to the imaging system.

error.defect_description: Tube logged against the wrong manifest line or a missing tube not flagged.

evidence.note: Specimens are collected at company centres or partner sites and shipped to the genetics laboratory; transit of one day is typical within Ontario and Quebec, longer for other provinces. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Check requisition, consent and specimen acceptability
steps.description: The assistant compares two patient identifiers on the tube with the requisition, checks that the provider signed the requisition and the patient signed the consent section, and checks gestational age for prenatal tests. The assistant also checks tube type, fill volume, haemolysis and days since collection against the specimen acceptance criteria.

error.defect_description: A missing consent signature or a labelling discrepancy is missed.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP specimen acceptance criteria; signed patient consent required on the genetics requisition by laboratory policy

next.condition: consent, provider signature, gestational age or eligibility form missing
specimen unacceptable: unlabelled, wrong tube, too old, haemolysed or underfilled

evidence.note: Consent signature requirement and specimen acceptability protocols are documented; the shares of incomplete and rejected specimens are estimates.

steps.name: Phone or fax the clinic for missing consent or details
steps.description: The assistant puts the specimen on hold in the LIS, phones the ordering clinic and faxes a request for the missing consent page, provider signature, gestational age or provincial eligibility form, and logs the call in the order notes. If the patient bought the test online, the assistant emails the patient through the portal message tool.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Common practice for incomplete genetic requisitions; times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the clinic to return the missing form
steps.description: The specimen waits in the hold rack while the clinic or patient finds and faxes or uploads the missing page. The cfDNA tube keeps for only about a week, so if nothing arrives the specimen expires and a new sample is needed.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: no reply before the specimen expired
order cancelled by the provider or patient

evidence.note: Reply times and shares are estimates; the stability limit of about seven days for cfDNA collection tubes is general knowledge.

steps.name: Check funding eligibility or payment
steps.description: The assistant decides who pays. For a provincially funded prenatal screen, the assistant checks the eligibility form against the province's criteria (for Ontario, a positive first-tier screen, age 40 or over, twins, nuchal translucency of 3.5 mm or more, or another listed risk). For private-pay tests the assistant confirms an online or centre payment in the billing system, and for sponsored tests the sponsor code.

error.defect_description: Funded code used for a patient who does not meet the criteria, or a paid order not matched to its payment.

control.basis: Provincial funding criteria for publicly funded NIPT (Ontario Ministry of Health program, and the British Columbia, Manitoba and Newfoundland and Labrador programs)

next.condition: not eligible for funding and not yet paid

evidence.note: Funding criteria and the online prepayment route are documented; the share needing a payment follow-up is an estimate.

steps.name: Phone the patient about payment
steps.description: A customer care representative on the genetics line phones the patient, explains that the test is not covered or the payment did not go through, quotes the private price and takes a card payment or a decision to cancel. The call and outcome are logged against the order.

error.defect_description: Wrong price quoted or payment applied to the wrong order.

evidence.note: Common practice for private-pay laboratory tests; times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the patient to pay or decide
steps.description: The order sits on payment hold while the patient decides whether to pay out of pocket or calls back after a missed call. Patients who decline are offered other funded screening through their provider.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Shares and waits are estimates.

steps.name: Accession the order in the LIS and label aliquots
steps.description: The assistant keys or confirms the test codes, patient demographics, gestational details and payer in the genetics module of the LIS, re-keying from the paper requisition where the order did not come electronically. The assistant prints barcode labels for plasma or DNA aliquots and routes the order to the in-house bench or to a partner laboratory.

error.defect_description: Transcription error in demographics, gestational age or test code.

next.condition: test sent to a partner laboratory (for example MaterniT or an Invitae panel)

evidence.note: Menu includes tests from partner laboratories (MaterniT, Invitae); the in-house versus send-out split is an estimate.

steps.name: Package and ship the send-out specimen to the partner lab
steps.description: The assistant enters the order again in the partner laboratory's web portal, prints its requisition, packs the tube to dangerous goods rules with a cold pack where required and books the courier for the daily pickup. The tracking number is recorded on the LIS order.

error.defect_description: Partner order keyed with a wrong identifier or wrong test.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations and IATA rules for UN3373 biological substances

evidence.note: Send-out handling is common practice for tests a laboratory does not perform; times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the partner laboratory report
steps.description: The specimen travels to the partner laboratory, which runs the test and posts a report to its portal. Turnaround depends on the test: about one to two weeks for prenatal screens and two to three weeks for multi-gene panels.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: partner reports no result or specimen failure

evidence.note: Partner turnaround times are estimates based on typical published turnaround for NIPT and hereditary panels.

steps.name: Receive the partner report and attach it in the LIS
steps.description: The assistant downloads the partner's PDF report, checks the identifiers against the LIS order, attaches the PDF and enters a summary result so the report can be released through the usual channels.

error.defect_description: Report attached to the wrong order.

evidence.note: Common practice for referred tests; times are estimates.

steps.name: Separate plasma and extract DNA in a batch
steps.description: The assistant centrifuges cfDNA tubes twice to separate plasma, or loads whole blood or saliva onto the automated extractor, in a batch of 24 to 96 samples, scanning each tube into the batch worklist so identity is tracked. Extracts are stored in barcoded plates.

error.defect_description: Tube placed in the wrong plate position.

control.basis: CCMG NGS guideline and CAP molecular checklist: sample identity maintained through the testing process

evidence.note: Sample identity tracking is required by the CCMG guideline; batch sizes and times are estimates.

steps.name: Quantify DNA and check extraction quality
steps.description: A molecular technologist reads DNA or cfDNA concentration from the fluorometer export, compares it with the assay minimum and flags low yields. Low samples are re-extracted from the backup tube or sent for a new sample.

error.defect_description: A low-yield sample passed through.

evidence.note: Failure shares are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare libraries or assay plates and load the run
steps.description: The technologist sets up the library preparation, array or genotyping plate on a liquid handler with controls, records reagent lots, and loads the sequencer or scanner once a batch is full. Prenatal screens run several times a week; arrays and panels wait for a weekly batch.

error.defect_description: Wrong index or plate position, or expired reagent.

evidence.note: Batching cadence and hands-on time per sample are estimates for automated library preparation.

steps.name: Run the sequencer, array scanner or genotyping platform
steps.description: The instrument runs unattended, generating sequence reads, array intensities or genotype calls for the whole batch, and writes run metrics to the run folder.

error.defect_description: Run failure or poor run quality.

evidence.note: Run times of roughly one to two days are added as the wait before the pipeline step.

steps.name: Run the bioinformatics pipeline
steps.description: The pipeline aligns reads, calls variants or computes trisomy risk scores and fetal fraction, annotates variants against population and disease databases and posts results to the analysis software. The wait before this step covers the instrument run time.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Instrument run plus pipeline time is an estimate.

steps.name: Review run QC and sample results
steps.description: The technologist checks the run against acceptance criteria (controls, coverage, call rate, fetal fraction) and reviews each sample's calls or risk result. Samples below thresholds are repeated or reported as no-call, and simple genotype and prenatal results go straight to the report.

error.defect_description: A borderline sample accepted that should have been repeated.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP: run and sample acceptance against validated QC criteria before results are reported

next.condition: prenatal screen, pharmacogenomic or targeted genotype with clear calls
sequencing panel or carrier screen needing variant review
sample or run failed, repeat library
no-call (low fetal fraction), new sample needed

evidence.note: No-call rate of about 3 per cent on first NIPT samples is stated; the other shares are estimates for the test mix.

steps.name: Report the no-call or rejection and request a new sample
steps.description: The assistant enters a no-result or rejected-specimen comment so the provider receives an interim report, phones or faxes the provider to ask for a new collection, and for online buyers messages the patient. The original order stays open, linked to the new collection.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Re-draws after no result are documented; time is an estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the patient to give a new sample
steps.description: The patient has to return to a collection centre for a new draw, usually within one to two weeks. Some patients decline, pass the gestational window or are referred straight to diagnostic testing and counselling instead.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: no new sample; closed with no result

evidence.note: Repeat sampling after a no-call is modelled in the source; the share who return is an estimate.

steps.name: Filter and classify variants
steps.description: For panels and carrier screens the technologist filters the annotated variant list, looks up each candidate in population databases, ClinVar, the laboratory's own variant database and the literature, and applies the ACMG and AMP criteria to propose a five-tier classification. Variants already classified in the laboratory database are carried forward.

error.defect_description: Variant misclassified or a relevant variant filtered out.

control.basis: ACMG/AMP 2015 variant classification standards, endorsed by the CCMG

next.condition: no new variant needing extended review
novel or uncertain variant needs curation

evidence.note: Classification standard documented; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Curate a novel or uncertain variant
steps.description: A senior technologist searches the literature and databases in depth for a variant not seen before, scores each ACMG criterion with its evidence, writes the classification rationale for the internal database and discusses close calls with the geneticist.

error.defect_description: Evidence misweighted, giving the wrong tier.

evidence.note: Source states about 30 minutes for a novel variant to a couple of hours for reported variants; the mode of 90 minutes per case assumes more than one variant or literature review.

steps.name: Confirm the reportable variant by a second method
steps.description: The technologist confirms each pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant with Sanger sequencing, MLPA or a repeat extraction, which waits for the weekly confirmation batch. Discordant results go back for re-extraction.

error.defect_description: Confirmation run on the wrong sample.

control.basis: ACMG/AMP recommendation of orthogonal confirmation for pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants; laboratory validation policy

evidence.note: Confirmation practice documented; batch cadence and times are estimates.

steps.name: Draft the report in the LIS
steps.description: The technologist builds the report from the template: result, classification, interpretation, recommendations such as genetic counselling or diagnostic testing, methods and limitations. For prenatal and pharmacogenomic tests the software fills most fields and the technologist checks them.

error.defect_description: Wrong interpretive comment or result transcribed incorrectly.

evidence.note: Required report elements are documented; times are estimates.

steps.name: Second technologist checks results and report
steps.description: A second technologist compares the draft against the instrument output, the requisition and the patient identifiers, checks gestational age and sex, and initials the check in the LIS before it reaches the geneticist's queue.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Laboratory procedure: independent second check of manually entered genetic results before sign-out

evidence.note: Two-person checks are common in genetics laboratories; the share returned is an estimate.

steps.name: Laboratory geneticist reviews and signs the report
steps.description: A certified laboratory geneticist or molecular pathologist reviews the data, classification and wording, edits the interpretation if needed and electronically signs. Normal prenatal and pharmacogenomic reports are signed in batches; panels with findings take longer.

error.defect_description: Error missed at sign-out.

control.basis: ACMG/AMP and CCMG: final interpretation and reporting by an appropriately certified clinical laboratory geneticist (FCCMG or ABMGG) or molecular pathologist

next.condition: classification or analysis to be redone

evidence.note: Certified sign-out documented; the return shares and batch signing times are estimates.

steps.name: Release the report to the provider, portal and billing
steps.description: The LIS sends the signed report to the provider's EMR over HL7, to eResults or by fax, queues it for the consumer health service where the patient has an account, and posts the charge to the billing system for private-pay tests.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: high-risk or pathogenic result needs a call and counselling referral
error found after release, corrected report needed

evidence.note: Results go to the provider and the portal; the high-risk share across the test mix is an estimate.

steps.name: Phone the high-risk result and refer to counselling
steps.description: A genetic counsellor phones the ordering provider about a high-risk prenatal screen or pathogenic finding, explains the next steps such as diagnostic testing, records the call and books or offers a counselling session for the patient.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Laboratory policy for direct notification of high-risk prenatal and pathogenic hereditary results

evidence.note: Counselling after high-risk cfDNA results and counselling included with Harmony are documented; call times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Missing consent, signature or eligibility form
exceptions.description: The specimen is held while the clinic is phoned and faxed; a few expire and need a new sample.

exceptions.name: Specimen rejected
exceptions.description: Unlabelled, wrong tube, too old or haemolysed; an interim report asks for a new collection.

exceptions.name: Prenatal screen no-call
exceptions.description: Fetal fraction or coverage too low; the patient is asked for a new draw, which adds one to two weeks.

exceptions.name: Private-pay order not paid
exceptions.description: The patient is phoned for payment; a quarter decline and the order is cancelled.

exceptions.name: Send-out to a partner laboratory
exceptions.description: Tests not done in-house are re-entered in the partner's portal, shipped and the returned PDF attached.

exceptions.name: Novel variant curation
exceptions.description: A variant not in the internal database needs full ACMG curation and possibly confirmation.

exceptions.name: Corrected report after release
exceptions.description: An error found after release leads to a redrafted, re-signed corrected report.

exceptions.name: High-risk result call
exceptions.description: A genetic counsellor phones the provider and offers counselling.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from specimen collection to report release

evidence.note: NIPT results within 7 to 10 business days of receipt (about 9 to 14 calendar days) plus about a day in transit; portal results 10 to 14 business days; modelled 10 business days. Panels and send-outs take longer; the p90 is an estimate.

benchmarks.population: Sequencing-based cfDNA screening, Ontario cost model

evidence.note: The model laboratory states about 3 per cent of Harmony cases give no result (dyn_prenatal).

benchmarks.population: Sequencing-based cfDNA screening, Ontario cost model

benchmarks.unit: business days after reception of the sample
benchmarks.population: Harmony and MaterniT at the model laboratory
The consumer health service online shop

evidence.note: Current shop price; the 2019-2022 price may have differed.
Stated by a vendor author; treat as indicative.

pain_points.description: Missing consent pages, provider signatures and provincial eligibility forms put specimens on hold close to the cfDNA tube stability limit.

evidence.note: Consent and eligibility form requirements are documented; the hold rate is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Batch cadence for library preparation and sequencing adds two to four days before any analysis starts.

evidence.note: Typical batching for sequencing-based tests.

pain_points.description: A prenatal no-call needs a new draw, adding one to two weeks at a time-sensitive point in pregnancy.
Orders are keyed more than once: paper requisitions into the LIS and send-outs again into partner portals.

evidence.note: Common with mixed paper and electronic ordering.

pain_points.description: Novel variant curation and geneticist sign-out are scarce expert time and form queues.

sources.title: Prenatal screening for trisomy 21: a comparative performance and cost analysis of different screening strategies
sources.publisher: BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth (Huang, Gibbons, Rashid, Priston, Bedford, Mak-Tam, Meschino)
sources.supports: Ontario model: publicly funded cfDNA screening available since 2014 for a subset of pregnancies (positive first-tier screen, age 40 or over, NT of 3.5 mm or more, other risk factors); funded cfDNA providers in Ontario are the model laboratory and LifeLabs; sequencing-based cfDNA turnaround assumed 10 business days from receipt; no-call rate 3.3 per cent on the first sample and 1.2 per cent on the second; cfDNA test modelled at CAD 400, genetic counselling CAD 250; women with a high-risk or repeat no-call result receive counselling.

sources.title: Standards and guidelines for the interpretation of sequence variants: a joint consensus recommendation of the ACMG and AMP
sources.supports: Five-tier classification (pathogenic, likely pathogenic, uncertain significance, likely benign, benign); results interpreted by a board-certified clinical molecular geneticist or molecular genetic pathologist or equivalent; evidence from population, disease and locus databases, literature and computational predictions; orthogonal confirmation recommended for pathogenic and likely pathogenic sequence variants; required report elements; laboratories should have reanalysis policies.

sources.title: CCMG practice guideline: laboratory guidelines for next-generation sequencing
sources.publisher: Journal of Medical Genetics, Canadian College of Medical Geneticists (Hume et al.)
sources.supports: Canadian laboratories shall use published variant classification guidelines (ACMG/AMP endorsed by CCMG); sample identity must be maintained throughout the NGS process; regions failing quality metrics are tested by an alternate method; professionals with final interpretation and reporting responsibility shall have appropriate credentials; laboratories may confirm variants orthogonally; reanalysis requires a request from the referring provider; VCF files kept at least 2 years.

sources.title: Genetics
sources.supports: Genetic menu: non-invasive prenatal testing (Harmony and MaterniT), carrier screening, pharmacogenomic tests (OptimalRx Plus), genetic counselling, hemoglobinopathy screening, Invitae comprehensive genetic testing, somatic tumour profiling, HHT, paternity and relationship testing.

sources.title: Prenatal solutions
sources.supports: Harmony, MaterniT 21 PLUS and MaterniT GENOME results available within 7 to 10 business days after reception of the sample; about 3 per cent of Harmony cases give no result and a re-draw may be considered; Harmony funded high-risk programs in British Columbia, Manitoba, Newfoundland and Labrador and Ontario each with its own requisition and eligibility form; requisition completed by a provider or bought online and signed by a provider; collection at the model laboratory centres or partner sites; results to the ordering provider and viewable on the consumer health service; counselling by phone on request.

sources.title: Harmony prenatal test
sources.supports: Patient must read and sign the patient consent section of the requisition; collection at centres in Ontario, Quebec or Manitoba; available from 10 weeks; results in the consumer health service 10 to 14 days after collection and sent to the provider; genetic counselling included.

sources.title: Harmony non-invasive prenatal test (online shop)
sources.supports: Private-pay price CAD 495 paid online; an approved requisition signed by the patient's doctor is required to collect and analyse the sample; allow 10 to 14 business days for the result to appear in the consumer health service; free genetic counselling included.

sources.title: Soaring demand for genetic testing highlights need for streamlined data interpretation
sources.supports: Variant interpretation takes about 30 minutes for each novel variant, a couple of hours for variants reported in the literature, and many days for the most complicated cases. Author is from an interpretation software vendor.

sources.title: Wages: Medical Technologist - Medical Laboratory in Ontario (NOC 32120)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 23.00, median 42.00, high 50.00 (2023-2024); Toronto region median 40.50.

sources.title: Effect of preexamination conditions in a centralized-testing model of non-invasive prenatal screening
sources.publisher: Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (Fibke et al.), abstract on BC Genome Sciences Centre site
sources.supports: 3,568 maternal blood samples collected across Canada and shipped to central laboratories; cfDNA quantity rose with blood shipment time in EDTA tubes, much less in Streck tubes; fetal fraction lower with higher maternal BMI.

sources.title: Licences and quality commitment
sources.supports: Brampton laboratory holds Accreditation Canada ISO 15189, Ontario licence and CAP accreditation; Impact Genetics holds CAP, CLIA and New York State certificates; Laval genetics and specialty testing holds ISO 15189; quality system includes specimen acceptability protocols, QC software, CAPA, change control, EQA and competency assessment.

assumptions: The test mix (prenatal 45 per cent, pharmacogenomic 15, carrier and haemoglobin gene 15, other in-house 10, send-outs 15) is the author's estimate; the company publishes the menu but not volumes.
Harmony is assumed to be run in-house; MaterniT and Invitae panels are assumed to be sent to partner laboratories in the United States.
The process starts when the specimen arrives at the genetics laboratory, but the first step's wait includes transit from collection, so the cycle time is measured from collection.
Instrument run time is placed in the wait before the pipeline step because system steps carry no hands-on time.
Patient portal publication is part of cd-portal-results and the patient charge is collected in fin-patient-billing; here they are only queued.

The genetic counsellor and customer care representative take part in this process but are not in the organisation file's process_map role list for gs-genetic-testing; they are taken from the organisation file's roles.

Volume follows the organisation file's driver of 6,000 orders a month, which is an estimate; with 40 molecular technologists in the organisation file the staffing is consistent with roughly 45 to 60 minutes of hands-on time per order across the mix.
Shares for missing forms, rejections, payment follow-ups, repeats and high-risk results are tier C estimates.
